key_insight: A GaOx hole transport layer can be made conductive in 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells through ion-exchange formation during co-evaporation, enabling strong passivation and high voltage without added Cu, Na, Ag, or heavy alkalis.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a practical back-contact interface strategy for high-efficiency chalcopyrite bottom cells, helping push CuInSe2 toward tandem-ready performance with a certified VOC above 550 mV.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap absorber via ion exchange.
Tested whether Cu addition, Na, and sputter oxygen flow affect GaOx conductivity.
Characterized the oxide as partly crystalline and evaluated device performance in optimized solar cells.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV for a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: GaOx conductivity appears sensitive to how the oxide forms on the back contact, so the process may not translate directly to all transparent or In-containing contact stacks.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
